title: Finance Q&A and Calibration Workpad — Optimize cost assumptions
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working Q&A / calibration workpad for the Optimize cost model assumptions that we will circulate to Finance for sign-off. It is intentionally messy — capture of the calls, quick sanity checks, and steps to turn the live spreadsheet into a finance-approved deliverable. The goal: agreement on data sources, calibration method, rounding/treatment rules, and the finance sign-off checklist by end of Feb.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Primary cost drivers: token processing (per-token compute), GPU-hour amortized per token (model topology + perf), instance overhead (I/O, orchestration), SRE/ops margin.
- Current working delta vs. last model: we reduced per-token GPU cost by 12% after applying batching/kv-cache assumptions; conservative scenario keeps a 5% buffer for tail latency.
- Open items for Finance: validation of reserved capacity discount tiering, treatment of capitalized infra vs. op-ex for Private deals, and FX adjustments for APAC regions.

Data sources included in spreadsheet (where each row in the assumptions tab points to source rows):
- Internal telemetry: token volume histogram (prod-api-telemetry: 2024-10 through 2025-01) — used to estimate sequence length distribution and batching efficiency.
- Serving runtime logs: average batch sizes and queue latency (serving-runtime/telemetry/export-2025-01.csv).
- Cloud invoices: GCP and AWS instance pricing + sustained use discounts (billing-exports/2024).
- Dedicated contract terms: sample reserved capacity discounts (sales/dedicated-sample-terms.md).
- Benchmarks: internal kernel-performance sheet and per-model tokens/sec (benchmarks/llm-throughput-2024-09).
- Public model memory & FLOP estimates: used to sanity check kernel selection impacts.

Calibration approach (stepwise):
1) Baseline per-token GPU compute cost = (GPU-hour price * amortized GPU-hours per 1M tokens).
   - Compute amortization derived from measured tokens/sec * effective concurrency during steady state.
2) Adjust for batching and KV caching: use token-length CDF to estimate prefix reuse and effective tokens served from cache vs. regen.
3) Add fixed instance/Ops overhead: baseline network egress, orchestration CPU, and storage IO amortized per request.
4) Add margins: SRE reliability reserve (default 8%), capacity buffer for peaks (default 12% for hosted), and finance recommended buffer (TBD).
5) Run sensitivity: low/nominal/high using +/- 20% on token volume, +/- 30% on batching multipliers, and +/- 15% on reserved discounts.

Current numeric working assumptions (from sheet "assumptions_v1" — these are preliminary):
- GPU price (on-demand equivalent): $2.40 / GPU-hour (nominal blended across regions)
- Amortized GPU-hours per 1M tokens: 3.1 GPU-hours (nominal), 2.7 (optimistic), 4.0 (pessimistic)
- Effective batching multiplier: 1.9x token throughput (nominal), driven by 65th percentile seq length and request concurrency
- KV cache hit rate (prefix tokens avoided): 18% nominal (sampled from top-100 routes)
- Instance/op overhead per 1M tokens: $12 (nominal)
- SRE/ops margin: 8%
- Finance buffer: currently unset (proposal: 5% for hosted, 10% for dedicated sales pricing)

Example derived number (nominal):
- Raw per-token compute = ($2.40 * 3.1) / 1,000,000 = $0.00000744 per token compute
- After batching/kv adjustments and overhead => ~ $0.0000064 per token (nominal sheet result)
- Important: unit in sheet is per-1k tokens for external reporting; multiply accordingly.

Open questions / decisions for Finance sign-off (needs explicit answers):
1) Reserved discounts: do we use the median discount from historical contracts (17%) or the sales-proposed tier floor (12%) for modeling future Dedicated pricing? Finance preference required.
2) Treatment of Private deployments: capital expenditures (HW + license) currently amortized over 36 months in the model; Finance: should we amortize over 60 months for on-prem deals to reflect longer refresh cycles?
3) FX & regional adjustments: APAC pricing in the model is multiplied by a 1.12 regional factor — acceptable to Finance? If not, provide recommended factor or regional table.
4) Rounding & reporting: final published per-token rates should be rounded to 2 significant digits in public docs; Finance to confirm rounding policy.
5) Contingency policy: for hosted customers we propose automatic auto-fallback to cheaper model variants during cap stress; does Finance want to treat projected savings from fallback as realized in baseline economics or as optional upside?

Fidelity & validation steps (what we will show Finance before sign-off):
- Link raw telemetry slices and the transformation query (bigquery path included in sheet).
- Show two-week rolling windows and how per-token GPU-hours vary by model and region.
- Re-run calibration with last-quarter invoice pricing to show sensitivity (sheet tab: finance-sensitivity-q4).
- Provide a simple reconciliation: multiply per-token cost by actual invoice for a closed customer (anonymized) to show model error margin.

Action items (owners & target dates):
- Aisha: prepare reconciled example for anonymized customer (due 2025-02-17) — sheet tab: reconciliation-anon
- Ravi: extract reserved discount history & propose three discount policies (median, floor, optimistic) (due 2025-02-14)
- Maya: run regional FX adjustments and provide recommended APAC multiplier by 2025-02-16
- Lukas: add tax and VAT treatment notes for EU customers into the model (due 2025-02-18)
- Finance review: schedule 45-min sync with Finance (requested people: Priya Rao, Dan McConnell) — target week of Feb 23

Checklist for final deliverable (Finance sign-off required items):
- [ ] Primary data sources documented + links included in sheet
- [ ] Calibration steps documented in a single doc (this workpad)
- [ ] Reconciliation example included and error band <= 12% between model and invoice
- [ ] Reserve/discount policy decided and encoded in sheet scenarios
- [ ] Rounding/reporting policy for public unit economics decided
- [ ] Finance sign-off captured in email thread or Confluence approval page

Notes from a quick sync with Engineering on 2025-02-12:
- Observed effective batching gain is higher on p99-constrained routes; we should separate heavy-traffic routes and tail routes in model (tab: route-segmentation).
- KV cache improvements slated in Q2 could increase cache hit rate by 7–10% — conservative model should not bake this in but include as upside scenario.

Proposed language to send Finance (email draft snippet):
"Hi Priya / Dan — attaching our working calibration sheet and a short reconciliation example. We are asking for two decisions: (1) which reserved-discount policy should be used for forward-looking Dedicated pricing, and (2) confirmation of amortization windows for Private/on-prem deals. If ok, we will incorporate your choices into the public Optimize unit economics page and capture sign-off on Confluence. Can we meet for 45 minutes the week of Feb 23?"

Unresolved notes (capture here so we don't lose the messy parts):
- Should we treat GPU preemption risk as an explicit cost line or fold it into SRE margin? Initial suggestion: explicit line for preemptible strategy, but Finance may prefer it in margin.
- How to treat credits/promotions during initial PLG adoption — currently modeled as separate "discounting" scenario, not baseline.

Version history / provenance:
- v0.1 (2025-02-10) — initial capture post-internal review meeting
- v0.2 (2025-02-14) — added reserved discount history from Ravi and first reconciliation
- v0.3 (2025-02-22) — incorporated Maya's regional FX proposal, added checklist for Finance sign-off

If you are reading this and want to edit the sheet: do not change the assumptions_v1 tab directly without a short note here — create a copy named assumptions_v1_yourinitials and add a short comment on the sheet.

Next sync: 2025-02-23 10:00 PT (cal invite pending).
